drivers.variant_notes: The 1979 production ROM set (750-07_1.716, 750-08_2.716, U6 720-35_6.716, sound 729-51_3.123) and the reference for this definition: GEN_BY35, six-digit displays (dispBy6), FLIP_SW(FLIP_L), lampCol 0, sound board SNDBRD_BY50.

A Bally/Oliver conversion ROM (one 2732 game ROM harl2732.u2 and a 2732 U6 720-3532.u6b, the same sound ROM) that widens the four player displays to seven digits (dispBy7); it needs seven-digit display hardware and otherwise drives the same machine. The catalog dates it 2004 and pinned driver.c's comment 11/02; at power-up it shows its revision, 090, on player 1. In the retained runs it fires the same thirteen solenoid-test outputs in the same order, publishes the same sixty lamps, shows the same forty switches in the switch test and fires the same solenoids for the same gameplay stimuli. The known-working table runs this driver.

PinMAME keeps a generic flipper column at internal column 11 (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL), which core_swSeq2m publishes at 81-88 (public = matrix index - 7), so public 81 is bit 0x01, CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT. The driver declares FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) with no FLIP_SWNO, FLIP_SOL or FLIP_EOS, so core_updateSw's flipper mask holds only the two lower button bits (82 and 84): it never sets this bit, FLIP_SWL and FLIP_SWR are zero so it copies nothing from the column into the game matrix, the synthetic flipper outputs 45-48 follow only the lower button bits, and whatever a host writes here is kept but never read. The flippers' end-of-stroke contacts are in their coil circuits, not MPU inputs: the playfield sheet draws an "N.C." contact across the upper winding of the left and right flippers (the upper left flipper's is unlabelled), and returns the upper left flipper's coil through the normally open "LEFT FLIPPER E.O.S." contact. The VPinMAME Bally library calls public 81 swURFlip and writes it for the staged right flipper key while its upper right flipper solenoid number is non-zero; core.vbs defaults that number to 34 and this table never clears it, so a staged right key does write 81. Nothing on this driver reads the bit, and in play holding 81 changed no output.

Public 82 is the right cabinet flipper button. The buttons are not in the switch matrix: the plug-connector sheet wires them to the solenoid driver (A3J2-1 R. FLIP. SW. (wire 10)), and each reaches its coil line only through a contact of the K1 flipper-enable relay. PinMAME keeps a generic flipper column at internal column 11 (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL), which core_swSeq2m publishes at 81-88 (public = matrix index - 7), so public 82 is bit 0x02, CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT. The driver declares FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) without FLIP_SOL or FLIP_SWNO, so core_updateSw raises the right flipper outputs 45 and 46 from this bit while the button is held and the relay (19) is up, and never copies it into the game matrix: the ROM never reads it. In play, holding 82 raised 45 and 46, and a tilt dropped them while it was held.

mechanisms.behavior: A one-ball game with no trough: the ball drains into the outhole between the flippers, closing switch 8, and the outhole kicker (public 7) serves it to the shooter alley, where the player launches it with the plunger. The ROM adds the bonus when the ball enters the outhole and counts it down, toggling the coin lockout (18), then kicks the ball and fires the drop-target reset (15) in the same step; a credit with the ball in the outhole starts the game, fires 7 and 15, and raises the gate (17) and the flipper relay (19).
mechanisms.label: Outhole and shooter feed

mechanisms.behavior: Four drop targets standing one behind the other on the right below the top saucers, A (switch 4) at the front to D (switch 1) at the back; the ball reaches each only once the ones in front of it are down. Each scores, advances the bonus and the Trotter fast break spinner value and spots the lit G-L-O-B-E letter; the second awards the 2X multiplier, the third 3X and the fourth 5X. The shared reset coil (public 15) raises all four: the ROM fires it at game start, with each new ball's serve and, with option S8 off, when the ball enters the target saucer; with S8 on only at each new ball.
mechanisms.label: Free throw in-line drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: A top right saucer that kicks the ball out (public 14) after scoring. Its first entry in a ball scores 25,000 (TARGET SAUCER 25K, lamp 53) and its second, with the in-line targets down again, a special (SAUCER TARGET SPECIAL, lamp 56).
mechanisms.label: Target (free throw) saucer

mechanisms.behavior: A top centre saucer ringed by the G-L-O-B-E letters. Each entry scores 3,000, spots the lit letter in the centre of the playfield, advances the bonus and kicks the ball out (public 13). All five letters spotted scores and flashes 50,000 and, by how many times the letters have been completed and option S32, lights the left outlane 25,000 lite, the G-L-O-B-E special lite or scores a special, then resets the letters, which are remembered ball to ball. Option S14 chooses between letters that keep scanning and letters that step one at a time.
mechanisms.label: Top basket G-L-O-B-E saucer

mechanisms.behavior: Five stand-up targets on the left wall, switch 26 at the bottom to 30 at the top, each scoring 300 and putting out its lite. Knocking out all five scores 10,000, advances the slam dunk target value (extra ball, special, 5,000) and relights them; option S24 remembers them from ball to ball.
mechanisms.label: Left side "Players" targets

mechanisms.behavior: A stand-up target on the right below the in-line drop targets. It scores 300 or the lit value, and when DUNK SHOT OPENS GATE (21) is lit it opens the free ball gate. Option S23 keeps its special lit for the rest of the ball.
mechanisms.label: Slam dunk target

mechanisms.behavior: A gate in the right outlane, powered by the continuous output 17: energized means closed. The ROM closes it at game start and each new ball and opens it (drops 17) when the lit slam dunk target is hit; a ball entering the open right outlane (switch 23) then scores 3,000, is directed back onto the right flipper, and the ROM closes the gate again. A tilt drops 17 with the flipper relay, so the gate rests open for the rest of a tilted ball, although the manual says a tilt closes it.
mechanisms.label: Free ball gate

mechanisms.behavior: Two bumpers in the upper middle (left and right) and one below them in the centre (bottom). Each skirt switch makes the ROM fire its own coil: 40 fires 9, 39 fires 8 and 38 fires 10. Lit bumpers score 1,000; all are lit on a three-ball game and they alternate on a five-ball game. The bottom bumper's cap lamp is 26 and the left and right caps share 42.
mechanisms.label: Three thumper bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: The pair above the lower flippers: switch 37 makes the ROM fire the left slingshot (11) and switch 36 the right (12).
mechanisms.label: Two slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: The left side spinner (switch 17) on the left wall beside its four value lamps (100, 200, 1K and 2K: 6, 22, 38 and 54), and the two centre spinners, left (33) and right (25), at the two ends of the centre spinner bar below the bumpers, with the SPINNERS 1 to 5 column (4, 20, 36, 52 and 5) and the advance-bonus lamps 51 (left) and 35 (right). A completed centre spinner sequence advances the bonus; option S16 lights both spinners or only an alternating one.
mechanisms.label: Three spinners

mechanisms.behavior: Two lower flippers and an upper left flipper below the left slingshot. The left button fires the lower left flipper, whose normally open end-of-stroke contact then fires the upper left one; the right button fires the right flipper. The K1 relay (public 19) switches the button-to-coil circuits: it is raised from game start to game over and dropped by a tilt.
mechanisms.label: Three flippers
